title: Delimited reply integrity — customer update and verification path
content:
TL;DR:
On 2029-11-06 between 02:14–03:47 UTC we observed intermittent corruption of delimited/structured responses (JSON and tabular payloads) returned from the hosted API. The issue caused trailing tokens or malformed delimiters in a small fraction of responses for customers using structured output formats. Impact was concentrated in EU-west1 and US-west2; overall token traffic impacted was ~0.4% but customers using strict JSON/tooling for downstream parsing saw up to ~3% of structured responses affected.

Why this matters to customers:
- Applications relying on machine-parsed JSON (webhooks, ingestion pipelines, SDK parsing hooks) could see parse errors, silent truncations, or occasional extra characters after the closing delimiter.
- This could cause downstream errors, retries, or degraded UX for end-users.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause (short): a race condition between continuous batching reuse and a new KV-cache reuse optimization introduced into the serving runtime. Under specific batching merge patterns the runtime reused a partially-invalid KV cache entry; that led to misaligned final tokens for some streamed responses, producing malformed delimiters or trailing garbage.
- Affected surface: hosted API text generation and structured output endpoints when: (1) continuous batching merged requests across tenants with similar sequence shapes, and (2) customers requested structured output delimiters (json, csv, custom). Private and Dedicated customers with pinned runtime configs were not affected unless they had adopted the same optional caching optimization.

Immediate mitigation (what we did):
1) At detection (02:25 UTC) we disabled the KV-cache reuse optimization globally for hosted clusters in EU-west1 and US-west2. This stopped new occurrences within ~6 minutes.
2) We patched the streaming assembly logic to validate closing delimiters before flushing to the network and rolled that patch to the two regions (completed 03:12 UTC).
3) We deployed a light-weight response sanitizer at the edge that removes trailing non-delimiter characters when strict_delimited_format=true is set (rolled 03:40 UTC).
4) We opened an incident bug (INC-12418) and prioritized a permanent runtime fix and additional unit/integration tests.

Customer-visible impact:
- Time window: 2029-11-06 02:14 — 03:12 UTC (most occurrences), with residual edge-deliveries until 03:47 UTC for inflight streams.
- Regions: EU-west1, US-west2.
- Scope: ~0.4% of total requests (all types) in affected regions; for structured-output requests the error rate among that cohort was ~3%.
- Severity: non-corrupt token generation (semantic model outputs) — only formatting/delimiter integrity was affected. No customer data loss or model parameter corruption.

Recommended customer actions (short-term):
If you are a customer that uses parsed/strict structured outputs, we recommend the following immediate steps:
- Enable on-client defensive parsing: wrap your JSON parser to accept a single trailing non-printable char (strip after final matching brace) and log incidents for analysis.
- If using SDKs: upgrade to SDK v3.4.2 (hotfix) which includes a local post-receive sanitizer that tolerates trailing characters and validates closing delimiters.
- For queued ingestion flows: add a short pre-parse verification step (e.g., check for matching open/close delimiters, reject and optionally replay).
- If you want us to re-run a set of specific request IDs for verification/replay, open INC-12418 with the request IDs and tenant identifier; we will run a controlled replay and provide evidence.

Operational timeline (detailed):
- 2029-11-06 02:14 UTC — First automated alert: elevated parse-error rate from customer telemetry (SDK telemetry + customer support notices).
- 2029-11-06 02:18 UTC — SRE/Runtime triage engaged. Initial hypothesis: streaming/assembly issue.
- 2029-11-06 02:25 UTC — Temporary mitigation: disable KV-cache reuse optimization in EU-west1 and US-west2.
- 2029-11-06 02:40 UTC — Patch: early delimiter-check inserted into flush path (canary on small subset).
- 2029-11-06 03:12 UTC — Patch promoted to full roll in affected regions. Metrics show parse error rate returning to baseline.
- 2029-11-06 03:40 UTC — Edge sanitizer (opt-in strict_delimited_format flag) enabled to prevent any lingering malformed responses to strict consumers.
- 2029-11-06 04:05 UTC — Monitoring: no new incidents observed; incident declared mitigated.

Root cause (technical detail):
- The runtime change was intended to reuse KV cache entries across closely-matched sequence prefixes to reduce token compute when continuous batching merges requests.
- Under a rare interleaving (batch A reused entry while batch B eviction/compact was concurrent), the resulting token assembly included stray cache bytes from a prior stream. Those stray bytes did not affect free-text outputs in a visible way often, but when a client requested a delimited/strict schema the trailing bytes could turn a valid closing delimiter into invalid output.
- The issue only manifested with a specific combination of sequence length distribution, batching shape, and the optional optimization enabled.

Permanent fixes and follow-up (what we will do):
1) Merge and release runtime patch that adds per-tenant KV-cache versioning and pointer-safety checks (PR in review: runtime/pull/833). Target release 2029-11-14 with full e2e verification.
2) Add deterministic integration tests that exercise delimiter-boundary conditions under heavy batching.
3) Expand our observability: new metric "delimited.parse_failure_rate" and a dashboard for structured-output integrity across regions (ETA 2029-11-21).
4) Provide customers an opt-in header/parameter: strict_delimited_format=true (already backported as a hotfix) which enforces extra validation at the edge for critical flows.
5) For Dedicated and Private customers: produce a runtime advisory and patch bundle; coordinate direct rollouts with platform eng and customer success to avoid surprises.

Customer remedies and remediation offer:
- We will proactively reach out to tenants we identify as having >0.5% structured-output parse failures and offer: (a) a replay verification run, (b) a log bundle for forensic validation, and (c) a one-time service credit proportional to the volume of affected structured requests.

How to verify if you were impacted: quick checks you can run
- If you capture request_ids: search for any responses that (a) fail to parse at the first-level JSON, and (b) contain any printable character after a final closing brace or closing bracket.
- Example heuristic (pseudocode): if rtrim(response) endswith '}' or ']' then OK; else flag and attach to INC-12418.
- Use the SDK telemetry dashboard in Console > Observability > Client Telemetry > Structured Outputs to see parse error spikes (we are surfacing detection signals there).

Communications and contact
- Primary contact: customer-success inbox (cs@redwood.ai) — include INC-12418 in the subject.
- For high-impact enterprise tenants we will assign a named CS lead and a runtime engineer for one-to-one support.
- Follow the incident channel for public progress: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-12418 (status page will be updated with final postmortem).

Closing notes (customer-facing posture):
We appreciate the disruption this caused to parsing-sensitive integrations. Importantly, the underlying model outputs were not semantically corrupted — this was a formatting/delivery integrity issue introduced by a runtime optimization. We have reverted the optimization, applied a sanitizer, and are building fixes to prevent recurrence while increasing observability so customers can detect and validate quickly.

Draft for status page (short, 1–2 paragraphs):
Between 02:14–03:47 UTC on 2029-11-06 we observed intermittent malformed structured responses in EU-west1 and US-west2 that could cause JSON/CSV parsing failures for downstream systems. We have mitigated the problem (rollbacks and hotfixes applied) and are rolling a permanent runtime fix. If your integration parses structured output please follow the verification steps above and contact cs@redwood.ai with request IDs for a controlled replay and remediation.

Action items for customer-success/ops (internal checklist):
- [ ] Send targeted email to impacted tenants with detection examples and the replay intake form (by 2029-11-07 12:00 UTC).
- [ ] Surface list of tenants with >0.5% structured parse failures to sales/AMs (by 2029-11-07 16:00 UTC).
- [ ] Publish final postmortem on status.redwood.ai and Confluence after root cause review (by 2029-11-15).
- [ ] Track runtime PR/QA and follow up when release is done; prepare customer advisory for Dedicated/Private (by 2029-11-14).

Prepared by: Aisha Banerjee (customer-success) — draft for review by Marco Liu, Evelyn Carter, Runtime on-call.
